name: Ben-abinadab
overview: Ben-abinadab was a male figure known primarily as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, responsible for governance during Solomon's reign. He held a position of authority in the city of Dor, as recorded in 1 Kings 4:11. Beyond this administrative role, no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-abinadab means 'son of Abinadab,' indicating a patronymic origin common in Hebrew naming conventions. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it identifies him clearly in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ben-abinadab as the husband of Taphath, as inferred from 1 Kings 4:11. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this mention.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-abinadab's significance lies in his role as one of Solomon's twelve appointed deputies, which highlights the organized and delegated system of governance under Solomon's wise and prosperous reign. His stewardship over Dor reflects the administrative divisions Solomon implemented to maintain order and support the kingdom. Although not a central figure in the narrative, Ben-abinadab's mention underscores the biblical theme of orderly leadership and faithful service under God's anointed king.
